newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times page one - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times page one - March 21.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:
* U.S. cigarette maker Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group acknowledged tobacco is addictive and causes cancer, and that companies have marketed cigarettes to children as young as 14.
* President Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin began a two-day summit in Helsinki, with both countries striking a conciliatory tone.
* U.S. House of Representatives voted by a wide margin to support a ban on what opponents call partial-birth abortions.
* Physicians who performed abortions said the so-called partial-birth abortion was just one option available to women seeking an abortion after 20 weeks of pregnancy.

* Hundreds of immigrants gathered outside a building housing the Immigration and Naturalization Service office in New York, worried about a misunderstood legal deadline which they believed could lead to deportation.
* American's growing trade gap with China could complicate Vice President Al Gore's visit to Beijing next week.
* U.S. Department of Defense researchers have found the genetic material from a deadly Spanish flu virus which killed millions of people in 1918.
* When Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko returns to the country next year, he will find a country where his power has deteriorated.
